headline: Riverside Community Garden Tomato Plot Dispute Enters Third Month, Mediation Scheduled
summary: Disagreement over 8-inch boundary overlap between plots 14 and 15 has resulted in formal complaint, counter-complaint, and one very uncomfortable potluck.
content:
What began as a friendly disagreement between neighboring gardeners at the Riverside Community Garden has escalated into what Garden Committee Chair Louise Beckman is calling "the most extensively documented boundary dispute in our 12-year history."

At issue: an estimated 8 inches of soil along the border between Plot 14, tended by retiree William Oates, and Plot 15, maintained by elementary school teacher Diane Prescott. Both parties have planted tomatoes in the contested zone, leading to what Prescott describes as "horticultural chaos" and Oates calls "her plants touching my plants."

"I measured my plot when I got it in 2019," Oates explained, producing a hand-drawn diagram with measurements noted to the quarter-inch. "I have been consistent. I have been precise. Her Roma tomatoes are encroaching on my Brandywines, and I will not pretend otherwise."

Prescott disputes the measurements. "I've been in this plot for six years and the stakes have always been right there," she said, pointing to a wooden marker that both parties agree "might have shifted" at some point. "Also, my tomatoes are Early Girls, not Romas. The fact that he can't tell the difference tells you everything."

The Garden Committee has scheduled a formal mediation for next Tuesday. Both parties have submitted written statements, supporting photographs, and in Oates' case, a 14-page document titled "On the Sanctity of Garden Boundaries: A Historical and Philosophical Overview."

"We've never had to do this before," Beckman admitted. "Usually when there's a boundary issue, people just... talk. Like adults. Over the fence. Apparently that's not happening here."

Other gardeners have been encouraged to "stay neutral and focus on their own plots." Several have requested transfers to the opposite side of the garden.
author: Janet Reeves, Community Correspondent
